rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Attaching له to تجوب lets the eye serve as the figurative subject; changing the order would obscure the metaphor and damage the description.
rows.anchor: أنه قال : ' تجوب له ' ، فعلق ' له ' ب ' تجوب ' لما صلحت العين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Preparation for a judgmental metaphor works like preparation for a metaphor inside a word: context must signal the comparison and open the figurative reading.
rows.anchor: هذه التهيئة وهذا الاستعداد في هذا المجاز الحكمي نظير أنك تراك في الاستعارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the verse about five clouds, the fingers are called clouds; the preceding thunderbolt, sword blade, and heads of peers cue the metaphor before five identifies the fingers.
rows.anchor: بل ذكر ما ينبىء عنها ، ويستدل به عليها ؛ فذكر أن هناك صاعقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the rajaz line, fires mean swords; rejecting justice and faith establishes the threat of fighting, so the image becomes intelligible from its context.
rows.anchor: وأن في ذلك دلالة على أن جوابه أنهم يحاربون ويقسرون على الطاعة بالسيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author quotes an unattributed line that sets sleeplessness caused by night against a sharp sword that lulls the speaker to sleep.
rows.anchor: ( ليل يصادفني ومرهفة الحشا ضدين أسهره لها وتنامه )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Two cited lines portray generosity or kindness as a bond that draws or binds its recipient.
rows.anchor: ومن وجد الإحسان قيدا تقيدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited poems describe Sayf al-Dawla's illness as illness afflicting the earth, valor, generosity, and the body's member called glory.
rows.anchor: ( ظللنا نعود الجود من وعكك الذي وجدت وقلنا : اعتل عضو من المجد )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The paired lines present spontaneous giving as generous conduct, while an excuse after being hurried resembles a culprit's excuse.
rows.anchor: ( أخو عزمات فعله فعل محسن إلينا ولكن عذره عذر مذنب )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lines portray steadfast generosity and resolve even when war and the meeting of swords put youth or gifts at risk.
rows.anchor: ( ماض على عزمه في الجود لو وهب الششباب يوم لقاء البيض ما ندما )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The paired lines match composure in battle with the temperament of a peaceful person despite a warrior's appearance.
rows.anchor: ( لقد كان ذاك الجأش جأش مسالم على أن ذاك الزي زي محارب )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited poets compare dawn's self-evidence with virtue so manifest that it needs no proof.
rows.anchor: ( وليس يصح في الأذهان شيء إذا احتاج النهار إلى دليل )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One line makes noble speech evidence of inherited nobility; the other says a person's deeds reveal lineage even without a claim about his grandfather.
rows.anchor: ( أفعاله نسب لو لم يقل معها جدي الخصيب عرفنا العرق بالغصن )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The paired lines call a place beloved or good when it yields an honorable aim or grows honor.
rows.anchor: ( وكل امرىء يولي الجميل محبب وكل مكان ينبت العز طيب )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A final line says even those who dislike a man acknowledge his virtue, and even those who do not practice astrology can recognize his good fortune.
rows.anchor: يقر له بالفضل من لا يوده ويقضي له بالسعد من لا ينجم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although ordinary usage seldom says that meanings are composed, it describes the same process as arranging, building, and linking meanings in the mind.
rows.anchor: وذلك قولهم : إنه يرتب المعاني في نفسه ، وينزلها ويبني بعضها على بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The analogies of weaving, embroidery, engraving, and craft concern meanings; therefore نظم likewise describes relations among meanings, not words alone.
rows.anchor: استعاروا النسج والوشي والنقش والصياغة لنفس ما استعاروا له النظم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A word has no identifiable place apart from its meaning, so ordering in speech begins with ordering meanings.
rows.anchor: لا يتصور أن تعرف للفظ موضعا من غير أن تعرف معناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Once meanings are arranged mentally, their words fall into place as their servants; knowing the positions of meanings in the mind is knowing the positions of their spoken expressions.
rows.anchor: إذا فرغت من ترتيب المعاني في نفسك لم تحتج إلى أن تستأنف فكرا في ترتيب الألفاظ

rows.speaker: أبو بكر
rows.claim: Abu Bakr is reported to have said on hearing the speech that it could not have come from a human mind.
rows.anchor: قال أبو بكر رضي الله عنه حين طرقت سمعه: أشهد أن هذا الكلام لم يخرج من بال

rows.speaker: عمرو بن العاص
rows.claim: Amr ibn al-As reports meeting Musaylima, who claimed Muhammad had been sent for grave affairs while his own mission concerned trifles; Musaylima then recited absurd rhymes and issued a rhymed judgment in a palm-tree dispute.
rows.anchor: قال عمرو: فأقبلت حتى مررت على مسيلمة فأعطاني الأمان ثم قال: إن محمدا أرسل في جسيم الأمور وأرسلت في المحقرات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author endorses Amr's judgment that Musaylima was a liar and says his speech has no eloquence, meaning, or wisdom that could rival the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: قلت: صدق عمرو. هل يخالج أحدا شك في ضلالة من هذا سبيله , وسقوط من هذا برهانه ودليله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author calls Musaylima's output base and says later comic writers' nonsense may be more coherent or easier on the ear.
rows.anchor: من السخافات أشف منه وأخف على السمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author adds an anecdote in which al-Asmaʿi says a man recited bad poetry to Abu ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlaʾ, who called it like a certain poet's verse.
rows.anchor: حدثنا الأصمعي قال: أنشد رجل أبا عمرو بن العلاء شعرا رديئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Scholars have proposed many explanations of the Qur'an's inimitability without settling its precise mechanism, but the continuing fact of human inability is unmistakable.
rows.anchor: لتعذر معرفة وجه الإعجاز في القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad challenged all the Arabs to produce a sura and kept demanding it for twenty years while denouncing their beliefs and judgment; they instead fought him, losing lives, kinship, and property.
rows.anchor: وقد بقى صلى الله عليه وسلم يطالبهم به مدة عشرين سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If they had the ability, they would have chosen the easy verbal challenge over costly war; as with a thirsty person who dies beside drinkable water, failure to answer proves incapacity.
rows.anchor: لو كان ذلك في وسعهم وتحت أقدارهم لم يتكلفوا هذه الأمور الخطيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh had intelligent minds, skilled orators, and accomplished poets; the Qur'an also calls them contentious and ludd, so their failure to exploit the challenge is evidence of inability.
rows.anchor: فقال سبحانه: {ما ضربوه لك إلا جدلا بل هم قوم خصمون}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Harmony in articulation is moderation among letter outlets, avoiding extremes of distance or closeness.
rows.anchor: والتلاؤم في التعديل من غير بعد شديد أو قرب شديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Harmony is perceived through ease on the tongue, pleasing sound, and acceptance by natural taste.
rows.anchor: يظهر بسهولته على اللسان , وحسنه في الأسماع , وتقبله في الطباع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When this sound harmony joins the highest clarity and sound proof, the perceptive listener recognizes the Qur'an's inimitability.
rows.anchor: إذا انضاف إلى ذلك حسن البيان في صحة البرهان في أعلى الطبقات ظهر الإعجاز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The universal challenge and the promise that they will never answer it make incapacity decisive; the author also cites challenges to a Qur'an, a sura, and ten suras as proof that Arabs and non-Arabs cannot match it.
rows.anchor: ثم قال: {فإن لم تفعلوا ولن تفعلوا} فقطع بأنهم لن يفعلوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author lists several aspects of inimitability: abandoning an answer despite strong motives, challenging everyone, diversion of intent, eloquence, truthful predictions, breaking customary patterns, and comparison with other miracles.
rows.anchor: وهي: ترك المعارضة مع توفر الدواعي وشدة الحاجة , والتحدي للكافة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Strong motives produce action when an act is possible; when people do not respond to the Qur'anic challenge despite strong motives, that failure shows they cannot answer.
rows.anchor: معارضة على القرآن لما لم تقع المعارضة دل ذلك على العجز عنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A challenge addressed to everyone makes it especially clear that people would not leave it unanswered despite strong motives unless they were unable.
rows.anchor: وأما التحدي للكافة فهو أظهر في أنهم لا يجوز أن يتركوا المعارضة

rows.speaker: بعض أهل العلم
rows.claim: Some scholars explain inimitability through ṣarfah, God's diverting people's intentions from attempting a response.
rows.anchor: وعلى ذلك كان يعتمد بعض أهل العلم في أن القرآن معجز من جهة صرف الهمم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rummani accepts ṣarfah as one aspect of inimitability: it lies outside customary patterns, like the other miracles that attest to prophethood.
rows.anchor: وهذا عندنا أحد وجوه الإعجاز التي يظهر منها للعقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Truthful reports about future events cannot arise by coincidence and therefore come from the Knower of the unseen; examples include Badr, the Romans' recovery, Islam's ascendancy, the challenge's failure, and other predictions.
rows.anchor: وأما الأخبار الصادقة عن الأمور المستقبلة فإنه لما كان لا يجوز أن تقع على الاتفاق دل على أنها من عند علام الغيوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rummani defines rhetorical homogeneity as related expressions sharing a linguistic root, and divides it into paired wording and semantic correspondence.
rows.anchor: تجانس البلاغة هو بيان بأنواع الكلام الذي يجمعه أصل واحد في اللغة والتجانس على وجهين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In paired wording, the response borrows the aggressor's word to stress equal measure, while the response itself is just recompense; the same pattern appears in verses about divine recompense for mockery, scheming, and deception.
rows.anchor: {فمن اعتدى عليكم فاعتدوا عليه} أي جازوه بما يستحق على طريق العدل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rummani prefers the Qur'anic pairing to Amr ibn Kulthum's threat to answer ignorance with greater ignorance: the Qur'an signals justice as well as returning harm, and the second borrowed term follows the first as a deserved consequence.
rows.anchor: ألا لا يجهلن أحد علينا ... فنجهل فوق جهل الجاهلينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In semantic correspondence, انصرفوا and صرف الله share the idea of going away: the people turn from remembrance, and their hearts turn away from good.
rows.anchor: فجونس بالانصراف عن الذكر صرف القلب عن الخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The paired root of turning suits both hearts, which move among thoughts, and eyes, which move among sights; both express movement or change.
rows.anchor: فالقلوب تتقلب بالخواطر , والأبصار تتقلب في المناظر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording links the increase of charity with usurious increase through their shared root of growth, replacing condemned increase with praiseworthy increase.
rows.anchor: وهو الزيادة إلا أنه جعل بدل تلك الزيادة المذمومة زيادة محمودة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the destructive day sterile implies that the punished will have no good after it; the metaphor is stronger than simply calling it ruinous.
rows.anchor: لأنه قد دل على أن ذلك اليوم لا خير بعده للمعذبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Stripping the day from night is more vivid than saying it emerges, since stripping suggests removing something tightly joined to its covering.
rows.anchor: لأن السلخ إخراج الشيء مما لابسه وعسر انتزاعه منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أَنشَرْنَا figuratively means that vegetation, trees, and fruits appear; the dead town is treated as resurrected, a stronger image than mere showing.
rows.anchor: أظهرنا به النبات والأشجار والثمار فكانت كمن أحييناه بعد إماتته

words: وتودون أن غير ذات الشوكة تكون لكم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الشوكة figuratively means weapon; it names the sharp feature that causes fear and thus hints at the relevant point rather than naming the weapon generally.
rows.anchor: فذكر الحد الذي به تقع المخافة واعتمد على الإيماء إلى النكتة

words: وإذا مسه الشر فذو دعاء عريض
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: عريض means great or plentiful, but width is more vivid because it is sensed; a reported alternative says breadth better signals length.
rows.anchor: الاستعارة فيه أبلغ لأنه أظهر بوقوع الحاسة عليه

words: وإذا مسه الشر فذو دعاء عريض
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative explanation says breadth is more indicative of length.
rows.anchor: لأن العرض أدل على الطول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The war is said to lay down its burdens, although the literal agents are its people; attributing their action to war magnifies its stature.
rows.anchor: فجعل وضع أهلها الأثقال وضعا لها على جهة التفخيم لشأنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Breathing means the dawn begins to spread; the image is stronger because breath brings relief.
rows.anchor: في التنفس أبلغ لما فيه من الترويح عن النفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The image means that God made the town taste hunger and fear; tasting conveys bitterness, while clothing conveys a continuing condition clinging to the body.
rows.anchor: لدلالتها على استمرار ذلك بهم كاستمرار لباس الجلد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being shaken is a metaphor for distress and is more forceful than other expressions for the severity of what afflicted them.
rows.anchor: وهذا مستعار , وزلزلوا أبلغ من كل لفظ كان يعبر به عن غلظ ما نالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pouring patience means granting patience; the metaphor is more expansive and clear than the literal wording.
rows.anchor: أفرغ مستعار وحقيقته افعل بنا صبرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Striking humiliation upon them means that humiliation settled on them; the metaphor emphasizes that it was firmly fixed.
rows.anchor: والاستعارة أبلغ لما فيه من الدلالة على تثبيت ما حصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase القصاص حياة states the benefit sought in mentioning life and calls people through desire and fear to obey God's ruling.
rows.anchor: إبانة الغرض المرغوب فيه لذكره الحياة؛ ومنها الاستدعاء بالرغبة والرهبة لحكم الله به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Compared with القتل أنفى للقتل, القصاص حياة is shorter, avoids burdensome repetition, and is more eloquent.
rows.anchor: والأول أربعة عشر حرفا , والثاني عشرة أحرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its letter transitions are more harmonious: fā to lām and ṣād to ḥā are smoother than the respective transitions from lām to hamza and alif to lām.
rows.anchor: فإن الخروج من الفاء إلى اللام أعدل من الخروج من اللام إلى الهمزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inimitability appears when multiple features combine to place the expression at the highest level of eloquence; a single excellent aphorism, such as Ali's, does not establish that judgment.
rows.anchor: فإذا انتظم الكلام حتى يكون كأقصر سورة أو أطول آية ظهر حكم الإعجاز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Brevity is eloquence when it conveys the full intended meaning; truncation is a flaw because it necessarily omits meaning.
rows.anchor: والإيجاز بلاغة , والتقصير عيي , كما أن الإطناب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Amplification is appropriate when detail serves need and interest, while needless length is a fault; the longer route is useful when it offers worthwhile scenery and benefits.
rows.anchor: فأما الإطناب فإنما يكون في تفصيل المعنى وما يتعلق به في المواضع التي يحسن فيها ذكر التفصيل
